root_cause.text: The ublk async partition scan worker dereferenced `ub->ub_disk` without taking a synchronized reference, allowing concurrent teardown in `ublk_stop_dev_unlocked()`/`ublk_detach_disk()` to NULL and free the `gendisk` before `ublk_partition_scan_work()` used it.
root_cause.evidence: The original `ublk_partition_scan_work()` directly accessed `ub->ub_disk->state` and `ub->ub_disk->open_mutex`, while teardown does `del_gendisk(ub->ub_disk)`, `ublk_detach_disk()` sets `ub->ub_disk = NULL`, and `put_disk()` may free it; the patch fixes this by replacing direct access with `struct gendisk *disk = ublk_get_disk(ub); if (!disk) return; ... ublk_put_disk(disk);` and changing `flush_work()` to `cancel_work_sync()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the deferred partition-scan work handler so ublk no longer performs partition rescanning through this workqueue callback.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the entire static function ublk_partition_scan_work(), including its retrieval of the enclosing ublk_device from the work_struct, the WARN_ON_ONCE() check and clearing of the GD_SUPPRESS_PART_SCAN state bit, and the mutex-protected call to bdev_disk_changed() on ub->ub_disk.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates a workqueue handler that previously performed deferred partition scan triggering for the ublk disk, so this code path can no longer clear the partition-scan suppression flag or invoke bdev_disk_changed() from that work item.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a safe deferred partition-scan worker that holds a disk reference, clears scan suppression, and triggers disk revalidation without racing teardown.
intent_record.what: A new static workqueue handler function, ublk_partition_scan_work(), was added. It retrieves the containing ublk_device from the work_struct, acquires a gendisk reference via ublk_get_disk(), returns early if no disk is available, checks and clears the GD_SUPPRESS_PART_SCAN bit in disk->state with WARN_ON_ONCE on unexpected absence, locks disk->open_mutex, calls bdev_disk_changed(disk, false), unlocks the mutex, and finally releases the disk reference with ublk_put_disk().
intent_record.how: This adds deferred partition rescan handling that safely operates on the disk only while holding a valid reference, preventing use-after-free during concurrent device teardown. It also ensures partition scanning is only performed when suppression was previously active, clears that suppression state, and serializes the disk-changed update under open_mutex before notifying the block layer to re-evaluate partitions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel and synchronize pending partition scan work during device shutdown so it cannot execute after the device is being stopped.
intent_record.what: The call to flush_work(&ub->partition_scan_work) in ublk_stop_dev() was replaced with cancel_work_sync(&ub->partition_scan_work).
intent_record.how: Instead of only waiting for partition_scan_work to finish if it is already queued or running, the function now synchronously cancels pending execution and waits for any in-progress instance to complete, preventing the partition scan work from running after device stop has begun.

grouping_result.intent: Remove the deferred partition-scan work handler so ublk no longer performs partition rescanning through this workqueue callback.
Cancel and synchronize pending partition scan work during device shutdown so it cannot execute after the device is being stopped.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make deferred partition scanning safe across device teardown by using a protected worker path and canceling any pending scan work during shutdown.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is specifically in the async partition-scan work handler dereferencing ub->ub_disk without a safe reference. Removing that deferred partition-scan callback directly eliminates the vulnerable code path.

The changes directly address the race in async partition scanning versus device teardown by making the worker hold a safe disk reference and by canceling/synchronizing pending scan work during shutdown, preventing use of ub->ub_disk after it is detached/freed.

candidates.rationale: This begins dereferencing ub->ub_disk->state in the async worker without first taking a protected reference to ub->ub_disk, matching the race with concurrent teardown.
The worker dereferences ub->ub_disk to access open_mutex without synchronizing against device teardown, so ub->ub_disk may already be NULL or freed.
This uses ub->ub_disk after no safe reference was acquired in the worker, directly embodying the use-after-free/NULL-deref race during teardown.
This is another unsafe dereference of ub->ub_disk in the asynchronous worker after teardown could already have detached and freed the disk.
Shutdown only flushed the work after stopping the device, which allowed the worker to run after ub->ub_disk had been torn down; this ordering contributed directly to the race.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the core unsafe use of ub->ub_disk in the async partition scan worker. The worker did not acquire a synchronized reference to ub->ub_disk, so concurrent teardown could NULL or free the gendisk before this call, causing the reported use-after-free/NULL-dereference race.

This statement dereferences ub->ub_disk in the async worker before any protected reference was taken. If teardown detached or freed the disk concurrently, this access could dereference an invalid or NULL ub->ub_disk.
This is another dereference of ub->ub_disk in the same unsynchronized worker path. It is vulnerable for the same reason: concurrent teardown could invalidate ub->ub_disk before the worker finishes.
This marks the start of the async worker path that dereferences ub->ub_disk without holding a synchronized reference. It is part of the vulnerable execution path that enabled the race with teardown.

The shutdown path synchronized the partition scan work only after device stop/teardown activity, allowing the async worker to execute after ub->ub_disk had been detached or freed. This ordering directly contributed to the race.

    Implement async partition scan to avoid IO hang when reading partition
    tables. Similar to nvme_partition_scan_work(), partition scanning is
    deferred to a work queue to prevent deadlocks.

This matches the root cause that async partition scan can race with teardown that NULLs/frees `ub->ub_disk`. The only teardown-side handling shown is `flush_work(&ub->partition_scan_work);` in `ublk_stop_dev()`, but it is placed after `mutex_unlock(&ub->mutex)` and there is no evidence in this function that the worker itself acquires a safe disk reference before use. The described fix would require synchronized reference acquisition/checking around `ub->ub_disk` before dereference; that is absent here. Therefore this commit introduces the vulnerable async worker logic and does not yet contain the fix.
